title: row25; allocator design defect, trigger written by us
live_proof: inspection with a line number in the 3.22.0 tree: memsys5 writes Mem5Link{next,prev} into the body of a freed block at src/mem5.c:143 (MEM5LINK), keeping only CTRL_FREE out of band in aCtrl[]. Design-inherent and never patched, so it is live in the pin and in every other release
object: a caller's block returned to the memsys5 pool, whose bytes become freelist metadata
lifetime_ender: sqlite3_free returns the block to the pool and a neighbour free makes memsys5 link and coalesce, writing in-band metadata through the caller's storage
fidelity: constructed demonstrator, real allocator. The trigger is ours, not an upstream input: it allocates two adjacent blocks, holds a pointer to the first, frees both so memsys5 coalesces, then reads back through the held pointer. That makes it the one case here whose consumer is the case itself, which is also why its probe site is in the case source and not in sqlite3.c. It is in the corpus because it states the corpus's premise: to ASan the whole pool is one allocation, so this is invisible at the layer below

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting, and since 2026-10-30 it is not scored as a catch either: this arm is judged by the mechanism rule the virtual arms carry in tools/arms.json (catch_causes), under which an access the mechanism did not reject is MISSED however the program then crashes. A SIGPROT(34) si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is MISSED with the fault kept in its note; a fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect and stays NO-READING:unattributed. What the rule rests on is the configuration and not a silence: SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP puts every SQLite allocation inside sqlite_heap[], sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool, and no free() ever reaches the guest allocator for a sweep to act on. The same harness with SYSALLOC=1 does emit allocator=system revoke=on-every-free on 31 of 33 cases (results/2026-10-29-cheribsd/non-nested), so the revoking path is live where it exists
